nytimes_articles.headline: Police Dept. Internet Site Is Not New York's Finest
nytimes_articles.abstract: Article discusses problems that have beset New York City Police Department's Internet site, which was activated on July 10 with high expectations; department officials comment (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Digital Faces Tough Market For Altavista
nytimes_articles.abstract: Market Place column discusses Digital Equipment Corp's decision to spin off Altavista Internet Software division; says it will not be easy for Altavista to command a premium, given performance so far of four other Internet search companies that have gone public this year; some analysts say Digital's principal aim is not to raise capital, but to receive more recognition for developing cutting-edge Internet technology, which could boost sales of Digital computers (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Latest Drownings Add To the Infamy of a Lake
nytimes_articles.abstract: Family of five and two others drown in John D Long Lake in Union, SC, where Susan Smith murdered two sons in 1994; were visiting monument erected in memory of boys when vehicle rolled into lake; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: From a Life Of Wealth Into a Life Of Danger
nytimes_articles.abstract: Michiko Kakutani reviews Joan Didion's latest novel The Last Thing He Wanted; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Karadzic Is Out of Sight, But Not Out of Voters' Minds
nytimes_articles.abstract: Sept 14 election of Federal Parliament and three-member presidency in Bosnia is haunted by presence of Serb leader Radovan Karadzic, who has been indicted for war crimes and is not permitted to run for office; while Karadzic no longer appears in public, posters bearing his image adorn buildings in Sokolac, Serb-held stronghold, in defiance of Dayton peace accords; map; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Chess
nytimes_articles.abstract: Robert Byrne analyzes games from this year's United States chess championship, Round 11 encounter between Dmitry Gurevich and Alexander Shabalov; drawing (S)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Stephen Manes appraises Compaq's new Armada line of notebook computers; drawing (M)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Martha Graham Dance Ensemble performs at Damrosch Park Band Shell in Lincoln Center Out of Doors Festival; photo; Jennifer Dunning review (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: American Air And Its Pilots Reach Accord
nytimes_articles.abstract: American Airlines and its pilots' union reach tentative agreement on new contract, ending two years of negotiations during which American executives refused to place any new orders or options for new aircraft; industry analysts expect airline to resume its traditional leadership position in industry upon approval of contract by board of AMR Corp, carrier's parent, and more than 9,000 members of pilots' union; details of deal with pilots are not released (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: In a Mine, a Paean to Danger and Daring
nytimes_articles.abstract: Former coal miner Chris Ledvina, whose legs were paralyzed in coal mining accident in 1978, opens coal mining museum at bottom of mine shaft in West Frankfort, Ky; facility is world's only museum at bottom of mine shaft; map (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Accord Is Sought by 2 Latin Trade Blocs
nytimes_articles.abstract: Two major trading blocs in Latin America, Andean Group and Mercosur customs union, will seek to join forces in free-trade agreement; Andean Group includes Venezuela, Colombia, Peru, Ecuador and Bolivia; Mercosur members are Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay; they will all meet in Cochabamba, Bolivia, where Rio Group of Latin American nations will hold its 10th presidential summit this week (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Christine Pascal, 42, Actress and Director
nytimes_articles.abstract: Christine Pascal, French actress and film director, dies at age of 42; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Fatal Shooting in Hospital Emergency Room
nytimes_articles.abstract: Woman shoots husband and wife in emergency room of Chippenham Hospital in Richmond, Va, killing the wife, before she is shot by police; another woman in room at time dies of heart attack (S)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Norman Harry Hollow, former tribal chairman of Fort Peck, Mont, Indian reservation, dies at age of 76 (M)

nytimes_articles.abstract: Recent account changes noted (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: Sensational Comeback for Cone: Seven Innings, No Runs, No Hits
nytimes_articles.abstract: New York Yankees pitcher Dave Cone, in first appearance in almost four months after surgery to remove aneurysm under right armpit, no-hit Oakland Athletics during seven-inning performance; reliever Mariano Rivera falls two outs short of completing no-hitter, giving up hit with one out in ninth, but seals Yankees' 5-0 victory; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: A Virus That Speaks Of a Deadly World Plot
nytimes_articles.abstract: Caryn James reviews tv program The Burning Zone, which has its premiere tonight on UPN, first of season's many X-Files clones; photo (S)

nytimes_articles.headline: NEWS SUMMARY
Seminarian Held on Bomb Charge at Airport
nytimes_articles.abstract: Roman Regman, 21-year-old seminarian, is arrested at Tampa International Airport following discovery of arsenal of weapons, including grenades and bomb-making materials, in his carry-on luggage; officials say explosives were powerful enough to have brought down USAir flight he was taking to Pennsylvania; he is held without bond on seven counts of possessing explosive devices and seven counts of possessing concealed weapons; Federal officials are exploring other charges; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Auto Workers Union Close to Choice for Final Talks
nytimes_articles.abstract: United Automobile Workers union officials say they will soon announce whether they will hold final round of talks with General Motors or Ford Motor Co aimed at producing national labor contract that union would then try to apply across the industry; current contract expires on Sept 14; union said to be leaning toward Ford, unless GM improves its contract offer immediately; job security seen as union's main issue in this year's labor negotations (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Smith Hurt as Bears Upset the Cowboys
nytimes_articles.abstract: Chicago Bears defeat Dallas Cowboys, 22-6; photo (M)

nytimes_articles.headline: Forces of the Future Win One, Lose One At the U.S. Open
nytimes_articles.abstract: US Open tennis tournament continues; Martina Hingis defeats Arantxa Sanchez Vicario and Steffi Graf advances in women's matches; Andre Agassi, Michael Chang, Thomas Muster and Javier Sanchez advance to quarterfinals in men's competition; photo (M)
